faq: Do you use customer data from other stores?
No. Pairs come only from your own order history and the rules you choose. We do not use data from other businesses, and we do not need customer names to find which products sell together.
Can I offer a discount on the pair?
Yes, from Standard. We set it up with your store's own discount tools and check that it applies correctly with taxes and shipping. You choose the amount, and we test it before launch.
What if I have few orders?
Then we start with pairs you choose by hand, such as a camera and a case. As orders grow, the data can replace or add to those pairs. We tell you how many orders give reliable matches.
Does this work with variants like size?
Yes. The shopper picks the size or color for each item before adding the pair. We test common cases, so a missing size or sold out item does not break the block.

desc:
A frequently bought together setup lets shoppers add two or three items that naturally go together in one tap. Ecom Swift LLC studies your order history, builds the pairs on your product pages and tests the whole path to checkout.

## Why pairing products helps shoppers

Many purchases are really sets. Someone buying a camera needs a card and a case, and someone buying a plant pot often needs soil. If the store makes them hunt for each piece, some will forget an item, and others will leave to shop elsewhere.

A pair block removes that friction. It puts the likely companion right beside the item they are viewing, with the price and variant already clear. The shopper stays in control and can ignore the block, so the help does not turn into pressure.

## What does frequently bought together mean?

Frequently bought together means a product page block that shows items which other customers often purchase in the same order, so the shopper can add them as a group. The pairs can come from your real order history, from rules you write, or from both. Each item still has its own variant, such as size or color.

## How pairs influence orders and revenue

A good pair raises the number of items in an order without making the shopper work harder. The mechanism is relevance plus convenience. The companion product answers a question the shopper may not have asked yet, and one tap is easier than a second search.

Pairs can also help low visibility products, because they appear in front of buyers who are already interested in something related. How much this matters depends on your catalog and your order volume. We therefore base pairs on your own data wherever it exists, and label results as observations, not promises.

## What a good pair setup includes

- Pairs chosen from real orders, not only from guesses.
- A clear block title and a short label for each item.
- A single add button that adds the full set.
- Variant pickers for each item, so size and color are right.
- Prices shown for each item and for the total.
- An optional bundle discount, tested at the cart and at checkout.
- Out of stock items removed from the pair automatically.
- Rules that avoid pairing items with very low margin or low stock.
- A layout that works on small phones.

## How we build it

We begin with an export of your orders and look for products that appear together more often than chance would suggest. You get a shortlist of pairs, and we mark any that look odd. Items you do not want paired are excluded.

Next we add the block to your product page template, set the pairs and write the labels. If you want a bundle discount, we configure it and run test orders through cart and checkout to confirm the price is right. We check variants, quantity changes and removal of single items from the set.

Basic covers pairs for a first group of products. Standard widens the range, finds pairs from order history and adds the discount option. Premium goes further with an order analysis report, stock and margin rules, simple click and add tracking and a period of adjustments.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Pair items that are used together.
- Keep the set to two or three products.
- Show the total clearly before the shopper adds.
- Test discounts with real checkout runs.
- Review pairs again when your range changes.

**Avoid:**
- Pairing products only because they are popular.
- Hiding the price of each item in the set.
- Adding the set without letting shoppers choose variants.
- Offering a discount that the cart does not apply.
- Using the same pair on every product page.

## Who this is for

This service suits stores with accessories, refills, kits or matching items, such as beauty, home goods, electronics or outdoor gear. It also suits stores with a few hundred orders who want to learn which products travel together. If you have few orders, we can start with pairs you define by hand and refine them later.

## What we need from you

Send a recent order export or give us access to view orders, and name any products that must never be paired. Tell us whether you want a discount on pairs. We work through collaborator or staff access and never ask for your password. We use only your own store data.
